published_Phoebis_Senna_rearing.source_table_inconsistency: native site parasitoid sum is 16, printed grand total is 17; Senna ligustrina three site sum 9, printed species total 7
limitations: Published observational counts; host species and origin confounded
Possible pseudoreplication of repeated larval records on the same monitored shrubs
No species-specific parasitoid probabilities or true cohort survival measured

source_grounded_host_augmentation.interpretation: A new documented exact host relationship changes both native and contemporary resource unions. The increase in native support can make a nominal added-resource count DECREASE even as more actual local feeding possibilities are documented. All-WCVP-region use remains unobserved extrapolation.

horticultural_pathway.independently_observed_cultivated_host: Senna polyphylla in south Florida, 2024 Phoebis rearing study
horticultural_pathway.contrast: Senna surattensis is introduced Florida in fixed WCVP; Senna ligustrina is native Florida
horticultural_pathway.interpretation: A cultivated alien host in Florida can be exploited by larvae while missing from the botanical naturalized distribution used to reconstruct anthropogenic larval-resource geography.
limits: Existence proof of a map coverage gap, not a global estimate
No evidence Florida S.polyphylla is naturalized; WCVP no record is not local garden absence
One study does not identify cultivation versus naturalization effects on abundance, parasitism or reproductive fitness

decision: Do not promote a new generalized ecological paper on butterfly fitness or colonization from these sources. The defensible mechanism hypothesis is that horticultural and naturalized plant introductions generate distinct host-exposure pathways with potentially opposing developmental and enemy-mediated demographic effects.
next_test_needed: Independent replicated site-level host occurrence (including cultivated vs naturalized status), larval host use, confirmed adult emergence and parasitism, standardized by survey effort; public presence-only interactions are insufficient.
